title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text: Spatial Data: A Primer

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
What is Spatial Data?

Data that explicitly represents location on Earth’s surface, typically through coordinates within a defined reference system.

Two fundamental types


Vector

Points (e.g., occurrences)
Lines (e.g., rivers)
Polygons (e.g., protected areas)


Raster

Continuous gridded surfaces
e.g., elevation, temperature
Each cell = one value




See Lovelace et al. (2019) for a comprehensive introduction.

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
Coordinate Reference Systems
The mathematical framework that links coordinates to locations on Earth.
\[
\text{CRS} = \{\text{datum},\ \text{projection},\ \text{units}\}
\]






Always check the CRS


Mismatched CRS is the #1 source of errors in spatial analysis. Use EPSG codes (e.g., EPSG:4326 for WGS84) to be unambiguous.
